The core innovation lies in leveraging event cameras to synthesize motion-aware blur, enabling domain adaptation without direct access to labeled blurred data. The method uses a multi-modal teacher network combining event and image modalities, followed by a student network trained on pseudo-labels generated by the teacher. Mutual uncertainty masking ensures robustness against unreliable pseudo-labels. The process hinges on two key mathematical constructs: (1) a motion-aware blur synthesis kernel based on event-driven optical flow warping, and (2) a mutual consistency check between teacher and student networks. The former bridges the gap between sharp and blurred domains, while the latter stabilizes learning in the target domain. Failure modes include misalignment between event and image data, overconfidence in pseudo-labels, and systematic errors in optical flow estimation leading to incorrect blur synthesis. These primitives form a closed-loop system where uncertainty drives adaptive refinement.
